If possible, it would be nice if fast-dds would detect sqlite3 provided by the system and prefer it over vendoring. And/or consider updating the vendored sqlite3, which is quite old already (released 2024), a newer version may have this issue fixed.

It seems fast-dds vendors sqlite3 version 3.47.2 which was released in 2024-12-07 ([chronology](https://www.sqlite.org/chronology.html)).

[Link to original](https://hydra.nixos.org/build/347318497/step/1/log) build log at NixOS/nixpkgs. Local copy: [fastdds-3.6.2.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33355809/fastdds-3.6.2.log) (view with less -R`)

See the build log for flags. Use GCC 16.2.0 on aarch64.

Other. Please specify in Additional context section.

new_candidates.body:
### The feature, motivation and pitch MuJoCo currently provides `connect` and `weld` equality constraints for closing kinematic loops. Although `connect` covers many use cases, modelling parallel mechanisms often requires hinge, cylindrical, or universal joints at the loop closure. Without these constraint types, one needs to restructure the kinematic tree or do some combination of joints and `connect` to represent the intended mechanism. For example, modelling an Agile Eye manipulator ([video](https://youtu.be/drwkExLdLMo?si=dZ1PwfBUmsv8JEXD)) or a planar 3-RRR parallel manipulator ([video](https://youtu.be/r7GSJtmRSy4?si=aDlSpnIwUDWape6N)) can require puposeful asymmetry while constructing the mechanism tree so that the loops can be closed with `connect`. A configurable 6D equality constraint would give users greater freedom to model parallel mechanisms. ## Proposed XML interface ```xml ``` The element would also support the standard `class`, `active`, `solref`, and `solimp` attributes. The `lock` attribute specifies which relative degrees of freedom are constrained: ```text lock="tx ty tz rx ry rz" ``` Here, `1` means locked and `0` means free. The translation and rotation are defined in the local frame of `site1`. A few possible configurations: Possible configurations include: | Constraint type | `lock` | Remarks | |---|---|-| | Weld | `1 1 1 1 1 1` | `site2` frame fully constrained to be coincident with `site1`| | Ball / connect | `1 1 1 0 0 0` | | | Hinge | `1 1 1 0 1 1` |`site2` can rotate freely about the X axis of `site1`.
Their origins coincide.| | Slider | `1 0 1 1 1 1` | `site2` can move along the Y axis of `site1`| | Cylindrical | `0 1 1 0 1 1` |combination of a slider and a hinge| | Universal (U) joint,
nominal Y–Z axes | `1 1 1 1 0 0` |`site2` can rotate about Y and Z axes of `site1`.
Requires careful implementation. Physically, U joint is two hinges in series.
First rotation can be assumed about Y axis of `site1`
and the second one about Z axis of `site2`, i.e., $\omega_{2\mid1} = \dot{\theta}_1 y_1 + \dot{\theta}_2 z_2 $. | A prototype is available in this [branch](https://github.com/v-r-a/mujoco/tree/equality_constraint_trial_byagent). Build from source or simply run the `simulate` from [build-general](https://github.com/v-r-a/mujoco/tree/equality_constraint_trial_byagent/build-general) directory with the provided example models. [Physx](https://nvidia-omniverse.github.io/PhysX/physx/5.8.0/_api_build/structPxD6Axis.html#pxd6axis) and [Newton](https://newton-physics.github.io/newton/1.6.0/api/_generated/newton.ModelBuilder.html#newton.ModelBuilder.add_joint_d6) support D6 joints (mostly via their maximal coordinate formulations). [Newton example](https://newton-physics.github.io/newton/1.6.0/concepts/custom_attributes.html#authoring-custom-attributes). The interface is similar to the proposed one. Additional features that are left out of the scope at the moment: - Limits for joints made by equality constraints - Stiffness, damping, and frictionloss at the joints made by equality constraints ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_
new_candidates.title: Introduce a configurable 6D equality constraint

new_candidates.body:
`LeRobotDataset.push_to_hub()` has `license: str | None = "apache-2.0"`, and the card template prints it as the dataset's licence. Most uploaders never change it. In a scan of the 3,000 most-downloaded Hub datasets tagged `LeRobot` (October 2026):

- 1,694 (56.5%, 51.9% of downloads) carry `apache-2.0` on an unedited template card.
- 305 (51.9% of downloads) can be matched to one of 65 public robot datasets whose terms I checked against primary sources. 201 of them (32% of downloads) declare a licence that differs from the original, mostly CC BY 4.0 data relabelled `apache-2.0` or `mit`, which drops the attribution and change-notice duties on paper.
- Another 45 (8.4% of downloads) declare a licence for data whose original release states none (for example the ALOHA sim demos and Push-T).

A tag on a copy can't grant rights the uploader doesn't hold, but downstream users read it as if it does. An independent write-up found the same default pattern (1,876 of the top 2,000 read `apache-2.0`): https://particula.tech/blog/open-x-embodiment-dataset-licence-commercial-use

**Proposal (backwards compatible):**
1. Keep `apache-2.0` as the effective default, but log a warning when the caller didn't pass `license=` explicitly (a sentinel default distinguishes the two cases).
2. Accept `source_datasets=[...]` in `push_to_hub(**card_kwargs)` and write it to the card metadata (`DatasetCardData(source_datasets=...)`), so conversions can point to their origin.
3. Optionally, have the conversion scripts in `examples/` pass the upstream licence.

I have a small patch for 1 and 2 (about 15 lines, no behaviour change apart from the warning) and can open a PR if this direction is welcome.

The scan and the checker are open source: https://github.com/s1g6r/rdq (browser version for any dataset: https://huggingface.co/spaces/rs1g6r/rdq).
new_candidates.title: push_to_hub defaults every dataset to apache-2.0, including conversions of CC BY datasets
